alalal-e81144-d1e104.summary: Rubric of Article 11: how differently faith is informed by its own form, by grace and by charity.

alalal-e81144-d1e115.summary: States the third question: how faith is diversely informed by its own form, by charity and by grace.

alalal-e81144-d1e124.summary: Objection: there is only twofold being, substantial and accidental (well-being), so there should be only two forms, not three.

alalal-e81144-d1e138.summary: Solution: faith involves three things: what is proper to it, which requires its own form giving specific being; the relation of its act to merit, its value for eternal life, which requires grace, which makes the person and his work pleasing; and the relation of faith to common perfection and the cause of all our works, which requires charity, the bond of perfection, directing all works to the highest goodness. Charity is called mother because it conceives all virtues in its womb, since the love by which we love God causes all the works and virtues by which we worship him.
claims: Faith's own form gives it specific being, grace makes its acts meritorious, and charity orders it to the common perfection of all works.
Charity is the mother of virtues because love of God causes all works and virtues by which God is worshipped.

alalal-e81144.summary: Article 11 explains how faith is differently formed by its own form, by grace and by charity, against the objection that there should be only two forms, for being and well-being. Albert distinguishes three aspects of faith. Its own form gives it specific being. Grace, which makes the person and his works pleasing, makes its acts meritorious for eternal life. Charity, the bond of perfection, orders it with all works to the highest good. Charity is called mother of the virtues because love of God causes all the works and virtues by which he is worshipped.
claims: Faith's own form gives it specific being, grace makes its acts meritorious, and charity orders it to the supreme good.
Charity is the mother of all virtues as the cause of the works by which God is worshipped.
